chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ أَخَاهُ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ فَيَطُولُ فِي التَّشَهُّدِ فَيَأْخُذُهُ الْبَوْلُ أَوْ يَخَافُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ أَنْ يَفُوتَ أَوْ يَعْرِضُ لَهُ وَجَعٌ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ

translations.en: About a man who is behind an Imam, and he prolongs the tashahhud, then the urge to urinate overtakes him, or he fears that something will pass him by, or pain afflicts him—what should he do?
He said: “He should perform the taslim, leave, and leave the Imam.”

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for someone praying behind an Imam who faces hardship during a prolonged tashahhud. If he is overcome by the need to urinate, fears missing something important, or experiences pain, he may conclude with taslim and depart without remaining with the Imam.
en.seo_question: What should a person do if he needs to leave congregational prayer during a prolonged tashahhud?

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the tashahhud portion of the prayer in which testimony is recited while seated
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: the urge or need to urinate
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: he gives the taslim to conclude his prayer
